title: Proton-pump inhibitor therapy induces acid-related symptoms in healthy volunteers after withdrawal of therapy
authors: Reimer C, Søndergaard B, Hilsted L, Bytzer P
population: Healthy volunteers aged 18 years or older without dyspepsia, heartburn or acid regurgitation in the preceding 4 weeks and without previous PPI or H2-receptor antagonist treatment
funder: The funding statement of the article was not read because the publisher page could not be accessed. Registry NCT00526006 names Zealand University Hospital as lead sponsor and lists no collaborator; PubMed indexes the article as Research Support, Non-U.S. Gov't.
result: Esomeprazole 40 mg daily for 8 weeks followed by placebo for 4 weeks, against placebo for 12 weeks: at least one clinically relevant acid-related symptom in weeks 9 to 12 in 26 of 59 (44%) against 9 of 59 (15%), p < 0.001; dyspepsia, heartburn or acid regurgitation at week 12 in 12 of 58 (21%) against 2%.
